subject: [NovaEdge] model swap + fallback playbook — throughput & error surge
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@novaedge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Kyle Ramirez <kyle.ramirez@novaedge.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: sudden p99 & error spike after v5.2 swap

Hi Karthik —

We flipped to Redwood model v5.2 with the new low-bit quant profile last night per the rollout schedule. Since ~02:00 PT were seeing p99 latency jump from ~800ms to 2.6s and error rates on inference calls up from 0.2% to ~4.8%. This is impacting our checkout flow (timeout retries causing duplicate charges).

Attached are a set of sample request IDs, the compressed logs, and a short video of the storefront behavior. Were live in US-West and currently on Dedicated pool id: ded-134.

Can Redwood pause the v5.2 variant for our tenant and revert to v5.1 immediately? We need a mitigation plan and an ETA for rollback or safe fallback.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of ML Ops — NovaEdge
attachments: novaedge-error-logs.tar.gz
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@novaedge.com>, Kyle Ramirez <kyle.ramirez@novaedge.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 & error spike after v5.2 swap

Olivia —

Received. Im pulling the rollout logs and the per-tenant routing decisions now. Can you confirm the exact variant id you saw in the request headers (model=redwood/v5.2:q-lowb-1)? That will speed things up.

Immediate steps from our side: 
- Rishi: start a scoped rollback plan (v5.1) and prepare canary traffic gating.
- Grace: check cache/KV affinity for your Dedicated pool and whether the quantized kernels triggered a path change.
- Ill open a temporary SLA exception request with Support/Legal if rollback will cause any interruption windows.

ETA: 60 minutes for initial triage. Well propose a runnable rollback/fallback playbook based on findings.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 & error spike after v5.2 swap

Quick findings from the first 30m:
- Confirmed variant header model=redwood/v5.2:q-lowb-1 for ~87% of recent calls.
- Error types: primarily 502 gateway errors and intermittent KV cache miss + eviction storms.
- Hotspot: an attention-kernel path in q-lowb-1 increases per-token compute under long contexts; this combined with cache churn explains p99 amplification.

Proposed immediate mitigation: 
1) Configure per-tenant policy to fallback to v5.1 for requests exceeding 1.5s latency or after 2 retries.
2) Disable prefix-caching for NovaEdge temporarily (reduces incorrect cache thrash).
3) Ramp v5.2 back to 0% for NovaEdge and keep telemetry for root cause.

I can run the rollback for the Dedicated pool once we have approval from the customer. Its a low-risk model swap (stateful KV persists), estimated impact: < 2 minutes of routing transition.

- Rishi
Senior SRE, Runtime
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@novaedge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Kyle Ramirez <kyle.ramirez@novaedge.com>, contracts@novaedge.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 & error spike after v5.2 swap

Karthik / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick triage. We confirm the variant id and approve a rollback to v5.1 for NovaEdge dedicated pool. Wed also like the fallback rule in (1). Please proceed — Kyle and I will be monitoring.

One ask: if the rollback will be disruptive to in-flight sessions, flag us immediately. We can schedule a short maintenance window if needed, but buying time is costly for us right now.

Olivia
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@novaedge.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:50:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 & error spike after v5.2 swap

Rolling update notes and playbook (attached): redwood-fallback-playbook-v1.1.pdf

Steps executed: 
- Initiated tenant-level routing override to default to v5.1 for NovaEdge at 08:30 PT.
- Activated latency-based fallback: if an RPC exceeds 1.5s or returns >1% error within a 60s window, route to v5.1.
- Disabled prefix-caching for NovaEdge and increased KV retention for 30m to avoid churn.

Current status: traffic on v5.2 for NovaEdge reduced to 3% (canary telemetry only). Error rate dropped from 4.8% -> 0.9% over 40 minutes. p99 back down to ~850ms. No customer-visible session failures reported since the override (so far).

Next: run a full postmortem once we stabilise; Lauren will coordinate an exec summary for NovaEdge and their procurement team.

—Grace
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Console
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@novaedge.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, contracts@novaedge.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 & error spike after v5.2 swap — exec summary + next steps

Olivia / Kyle / contracts@novaedge.com —

Executive summary (for your stakeholders): 
- Impact window: 2026-12-01 01:50 PT -> 2026-12-01 09:10 PT (root cause mitigation begun 08:30 PT).
- Root cause (summary): aggressive low-bit quantization path in v5.2 (q-lowb-1) introduced a fallback attention kernel that increases per-token work for long contexts, which combined with tenant cache evictions produced p99 amplification and gateway errors under NovaEdges traffic pattern.
- Actions taken: tenant-level rollback to v5.1, latency-based automatic fallback policy, prefix-caching disabled, KV retention increased.
- Outcome: error rate reduced to <1%, p99 restored to baseline (~800–900ms). No data exposure.

Proposed follow-ups (next 72 hours): 
1) Joint postmortem doc (Redwood + NovaEdge) — draft in 24 hours.
2) Model-validation checklist update: add synthetic long-context perf regression tests with q-profile variants.
3) Consider a delayed canary for q-lowb profiles with smaller concurrency gates and wider telemetry windows.
4) SLA exception approval: well submit paperwork if NovaEdge requires credit for the incident window.

Ive attached a formal playbook and the SLA exception request document. Please let me know if you want an exec call tomorrow; were available 10–12 PT.

Thanks for the partnership and patience — were prioritising preventing recurrence.

—Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success Operations
attachments: redwood-fallback-playbook-v1.1.pdf, sla-exception-request.docx
